conclusion: On the fixed XY0_Z2 mesh, the diagnostic current-work branch has solved 6.0, 6.5, 7.0, 7.5 and 8.0 V fields; its 6 V heat power and sampled peak temperature are lower than the original drift-heat control.

panels.definition: Maximum temperature rise over the 5x5x5 element sampling points

same_mesh_figure.curve_semantics: Both series are NT. The heat-source definitions differ; these are not linear-versus-nonlinear labels.

reference_layout_figure.LQ: Original drift-heat three-stage no-return-feedback LQ reference, L0 mesh; 3 V metrics scaled by V for E and V^2 for temperature/heat. Not independently solved half-volt cases and not a current-work LQ model.
reference_layout_figure.comparison_limit: LQ and NT current-work branches have different heat-source definitions and different meshes. The figure is a reference overview, not a controlled nonlinearity comparison.
reference_layout_figure.original_NT: Only the accepted same-mesh 6 V control is shown. Failed fold states and uncomputed original-model high-voltage points are omitted.

integrity.lines: Straight connections between actual NT points guide the eye only
integrity.acceptance: PASS_NOT_MESH_ACCEPTANCE; physical model uncalibrated; electrical-work gap 2.52-2.97% is not an accepted closure certificate
integrity.replicates: Deterministic numerical cases, one archived state per plotted voltage; no statistical error bars
integrity.temperature_comparison: Peak/source ratio is descriptive of each solved source distribution, not a material constant or an isolated causal experiment.
